title: Jerusalem's Sins and the Smelting Pot

questions.question: Ezekiel is asked to judge the "city of..."?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:2 (ESV): "And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Then declare to her all her abominations."

questions.question: What action brought Jerusalem to its day of doom?
options: Shedding blood in its midst and making idols for itself
Refusing to pay the temple tax
Rebelling against the king of Assyria
Building walls too high around the city
questions.correctAnswer: Shedding blood in its midst and making idols for itself
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:3 (ESV): "A city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her time may come, and that makes idols to defile herself!"

questions.question: What are the princes of Israel in Jerusalem bent on?
options: Each is bent on shedding blood, according to his power
Storing up wealth in their storehouses
Worshiping all the gods of the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: Each is bent on shedding blood, according to his power
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:6 (ESV): "Behold, the princes of Israel in you, every one according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood."

questions.question: Which of the following describes the sins committed in Jerusalem according to verses 7-12?
options: Treating father and mother with contempt
Extorting the sojourner and wronging the fatherless and widow
Profaning the Sabbaths and committing sexual abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:7-12 enumerates these specific sins: father, mother, sojourner, widow, sabbath, uncleanness, incest, bribery, extortion.

questions.question: God says, "Behold, I strike my hands together at the dishonest gain that you have made, and at the... that has been in your midst."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:13 (ESV): "Behold, I strike my hands together at the dishonest gain that you have made, and at the blood that has been in your midst."

questions.question: To what does the Lord compare the house of Israel in verse 18?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:18 (ESV): "Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me; all of them are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the furnace; they are dross of silver."

questions.question: Because they have all become dross, where will God gather them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:19 (ESV): "Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem."

questions.question: Just as silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin are gathered into a furnace to be blown upon with fire and melted, so God will gather them in His anger and melt them in Jerusalem. What does this represent?
options: The Babylonian siege and destruction of Jerusalem
A literal volcano erupting in Judah
The purification of the Levitical priests
The final judgment at the end of days
questions.correctAnswer: The Babylonian siege and destruction of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:20-22 (ESV): "I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst of it..." Symbolizing the fiery ordeal of the siege and burning of the city.

questions.question: God describes a conspiracy of whom in the midst of the land? "Like a roaring lion tearing the prey, they have devoured human lives..."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:25 (ESV): "The conspiracy of her prophets in her midst is like a roaring lion tearing the prey; they have devoured human lives..."

questions.question: Who have done violence to God's law and profaned His holy things, making no distinction between holy and common?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:26 (ESV): "Her priests have done violence to my law and have profaned my holy things. They have made no distinction between the holy and the common,"

questions.question: Who are like wolves tearing the prey, shedding blood, destroying lives to get dishonest gain?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:27 (ESV): "Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, shedding blood, destroying lives to get dishonest gain."

questions.question: Who smeared whitewash on behalf of the princes, seeing false visions and divining lies for them?
options: The women who weep for Tammuz
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:28 (ESV): "And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord God,' when the Lord has not spoken."

questions.question: Who practiced extortion, committed robbery, oppressed the poor and needy, and extorted the sojourner without justice?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:29 (ESV): "The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy, and have extorted from the sojourner without justice."

questions.question: What did God seek for among them, but found no one?
options: A man who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before Him for the land, that He should not destroy it
A prophet to speak truth like Jeremiah
Ten righteous men to spare the city like Sodom
A king who would repent like Josiah
questions.correctAnswer: A man who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before Him for the land, that He should not destroy it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:30 (ESV): "And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none."

questions.question: Because God found no one to stand in the breach, what did He pour out upon them?
options: His indignation; He consumed them with the fire of His wrath
A flood of water from the heavens
A plague of locusts that ate every green thing
Silence and darkness for forty years
questions.correctAnswer: His indignation; He consumed them with the fire of His wrath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:31 (ESV): "Therefore I have poured out my indignation upon them. I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have returned their way upon their heads, declares the Lord God."

key_verse_text: "And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none."
